# Workflow Policy Registry

**Version**: 1.24.0 | **Generated by**: autoharness

This registry is the authoritative source for cross-agent workflow policies. Each policy declares the agents it governs, the gate point where it is enforced, the preconditions that must be true before the agent may act, the postconditions that must hold before control advances, and the action to take on violation.

Agents must read this file at each declared gate point and enforce the relevant policy before proceeding.

---

## P-001: Single-Release-Unit Completion

| Field      | Value                          |
|------------|--------------------------------|
| Policy ID  | P-001                          |
| Applies To | `ship`           |
| Gate Point | Pre-flight (Step 1)            |

**Statement**: The ship agent must complete one top-level release unit (feature or chore) through PR merge **and any required post-merge release closure** before starting a new one. When `feature_shipments` is `true`, a merged release unit remains in-flight until Ship Step 5 has finished any required tag, publish, release-record, or post-merge closure-branch work. Parallel in-flight release units create branch conflicts, context fragmentation, and agent interference.

**Precondition**: No backlog tasks with status `Active` exist under any top-level work item other than the current feature or chore, and no previously merged top-level release unit is still awaiting required post-merge release closure (for example, an open post-merge closure branch/PR, a missing tag, or a pending publish step when `feature_shipments` is `true`).

**Postcondition**: All tasks under the current top-level work item are `Done`, and any required post-merge release closure is complete, before the orchestrator claims work on a new feature or chore.

**Violation Action**: Halt. Do not proceed until the conflict is resolved or the operator explicitly overrides with `skip_policy: P-001`.

## P-002: TDD Gate (Harness-Satisfied Precondition)

| Field      | Value                                                        |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| Policy ID  | P-002                                                        |
| Applies To | `ship` (wave scheduler, queue consumer, and claim-time gate), `harness-architect` skill (producer / no-scaffold partition), `build-feature` skill (dispatch consumer and pre-work precondition probe) |
| Gate Point | Per-wave static intake at Ship Step 2 / Step 2a and harness-architect Step 1a, re-entered once per wave from Ship Step 4.0 (P-002.6); claim-time re-evaluation at Ship Step 4.1a; pre-work probe at build-feature Step 0; per-wave convergence at Ship Step 4.6; read-only command screening (P-002.5) immediately before either command is ever executed |

**Statement**: The ship agent may only claim and implement a task once that task is
**harness-satisfied**. A task is harness-satisfied when the harness-architect has confirmed that
its test harness compiles and all of its tests fail in the red phase, or when it carries a
`harness-exempt` declaration that passes every P-002.1 condition **at the gate that owns that
condition** — static conditions at intake, predecessor red evidence at claim time.

**Precondition** (ship): The task carries the `harness-ready` label, **or** the task carries the
`harness-exempt` label and is P-002.1-valid at the gate being evaluated.

**Postcondition** (harness-architect), **stated per wave** (P-002.6): every task in the **current
wave** has the `harness-ready` label, its harness compiles (`go test -run=^$ -count=1 ./...`), and
all of its tests fail with expected failure markers — **before any task in that wave is
implemented**. The whole wave is therefore red simultaneously; each member is then driven green
against its **own scoped verification command**, and the wave's full-suite convergence gate runs
once, after every member is individually green (P-002.6, *Wave green semantics*). A P-002.1-valid
`harness-exempt` task scaffolds no harness test function, so this postcondition holds vacuously for
it and no `harness-ready` label is applied. The global form — every task in the release unit is
harness-satisfied before its own implementation — is the **union over waves** and is entailed by
the per-wave form, because a wave is admitted only after every one of its dependencies is terminal.

**Why the postcondition is per-wave.** Scaffolding the whole shipment in one up-front pass is not
merely slower, it is **unsatisfiable** on any DAG where a harness must compile against a
declaration that a *predecessor task* has not yet implemented. The predecessor cannot be
implemented before its own harness exists, and its dependent's harness cannot compile before the
predecessor lands. One pass has no ordering that satisfies both. Waves break the cycle by
ordering, never by weakening the gate: see P-002.6.

**Enforcement** (ship): For the current wave only, filter the ready queue to harness-satisfied
tasks — those carrying `harness-ready`, plus those carrying `harness-exempt` that pass P-002.1
**static intake**. Evaluate the static conditions **before** admitting the task; an unevaluated
`harness-exempt` label is not admission. Re-evaluate the claim-time conditions in P-002.1
immediately before the task is claimed.

**Violation Action**: Halt and report the gap. For a task carrying neither label, suggest running
the harness-architect. For a task whose `harness-exempt` declaration fails P-002.1, report a
P-002 gap using the P-002.2 taxonomy and do not scaffold a substitute harness.

---

### P-002.1 — Harness-Exempt Alternative Satisfaction (Fail-Closed)

**Statement**: `harness-exempt` is an alternative way to satisfy P-002, never a way to skip it.
The label on its own grants nothing. A task is P-002.1-valid only when every condition below
holds. If any condition is missing, unreadable, ambiguous, or unrecognized, the task is **not**
harness-satisfied — fail closed.

**Recognized exemption classes** (closed vocabulary; no other value is recognized):

| Class | Applies to | Predecessor harness owner |
|---|---|---|
| `docs-only` | Changes documentation, instruction, prompt, or agent artifacts only; no production or test code | Not required |
| `verification-only` | Executes and records evidence for behavior that already shipped or is delivered by a prerequisite; commits only green guards and evidence artifacts, never a new red assertion | Not required |
| `covered-by` | Behavior-changing implementation whose failing harness is owned by an existing predecessor task named in `harness_owner` | **Required** |

**There is no `declaration-only` class (cycle-29).** A task that lands a production declaration —
an exported type, a serialized struct field, a function or method signature, a sentinel, or any
other symbol a caller can observe — is **behavior-changing production code** and is a **normal
harness-required task**. It carries `harness-ready`, not `harness-exempt`. Declaring an exemption
class for it was a carve-out from Constitution Principle II (Test-First Development), which is
NON-NEGOTIABLE and admits no carve-out; the class is withdrawn rather than deviated from.

**How a declaration task gets a genuinely red harness** — the objection the class was invented to
answer is real but has a correct answer. A test that fails *only because a symbol does not exist*
is a build error, and P-004 does not accept a build error as a red phase. A **source-shape
harness** avoids both horns: it asserts over the package's own source text through `go/parser` and
`go/ast` (or the equivalent structural probe for a non-Go surface) rather than referencing the
missing symbol. Such a harness

* **compiles cleanly before the declaration exists**, because it names no undeclared identifier —
  it imports only `go/ast`, `go/parser`, `go/token`, and `testing`; and
* **fails on an assertion**, not on a build error — "`RemediationIntent` struct is not declared in
  `checkpoint_schema.go`", "`CheckpointSummary` has no field tagged `json:\"remediation_intent\"`";
  and
* **turns green only when the implementation lands the declared shape**, so it is a real gate and
  not a tautology.

This satisfies P-002's harness-compiles postcondition and P-004's red-phase requirement
simultaneously, with no exemption and no Principle II deviation. Every declaration task in a plan
MUST carry one. Fabricating a test that references the missing symbol remains forbidden — that is
the build error P-004 rejects, and it is not what this rule authorizes.

**Ordering is fixed: harness first, declaration second (cycle-31).** The source-shape harness is
not merely *required*, it **lands before** the declaration it gates. Landing a production stub
first "so the package compiles", then the harness, then the implementation, is the same Principle
II carve-out by another route: the stub is observable production surface admitted with **no**
observed failing test. Because a source-shape harness compiles against the pre-declaration tree by
construction, such a stub is never necessary. No agent may scaffold, request, or accept a
production stub ahead of the harness that gates it — `harness-architect` writes none, and a plan or
task instructing one is a **plan defect to report** (`EXEMPT_BEHAVIOR_NO_OWNER` when it is dressed
as an exemption; otherwise a P-002 gap), never an instruction to follow.

**Behaviour beyond the declared shape needs its own prior red.** A task may land a declaration and
its behaviour in one green step only when that behaviour is either

* turned green by that same commit and retained as a green-step regression guard, or
* owned by a **named later task** whose behaviour harness lands in a strictly later wave, against
  the landed declaration.

A **seam or declaration whose body would absorb real behaviour** — reading, mutating, or writing —
MUST be split into *declaration* → *behaviour harness* → *implementation*, each gated by a harness
that precedes it. There is no stub loophole in either direction: not a stub ahead of the harness,
and not behaviour riding into the tree behind a shape-only red.

**Required exemption metadata** — all of the following MUST be present and machine-readable:

1. The `harness-exempt` label on the task.
2. A **harness exemption contract block** in the task body, delimited by
   `<!-- BEGIN:harness-exemption-contract -->` and `<!-- END:harness-exemption-contract -->`, whose
   fenced body carries these five canonical keys, one per line, in this order and with this exact
   grammar (`key: value`, lowercase snake_case keys, no surrounding quotes):

   ```text
   harness_exemption_class: <docs-only|verification-only|covered-by>
   harness_exemption_reason: <one line of text>
   harness_owner: <task-id|none>
   exempt_verification_command: <exact command>
   exempt_precondition: must-fail-before-deliverable
   ```

3. Representation in the declared task/plan contract: the governing plan, feature, or shipment
   contract enumerates a closed exempt set, and this task is a member of it.
4. For `covered-by` only, a sixth key appended after `exempt_precondition`:
   `harness_owner_command: <exact command>` — the predecessor owner's harness command, which is
   the command the implementation loop runs. The five canonical keys stay contiguous and in the
   same order on every exempt task; the sixth is appended so the shared grammar is identical
   across classes.

The contract block is body metadata, not frontmatter. The backlog artifact frontmatter contract
(`.backlogit/header-def.yaml`) declares a closed per-type field set that does not include these
keys, so placing them in frontmatter would be rejected or silently dropped. The block is the
authoritative, greppable location; prose restatements are advisory.

**Key rules**:

* `harness_exemption_class` MUST be exactly one of the three class tokens. `covered-by` carries no
  inline owner ID — the owner belongs in `harness_owner`. `declaration-only` is **not** a token;
  a task declaring it is `EXEMPT_CLASS_UNRECOGNIZED` (fail closed), because the class was
  withdrawn in cycle 29.
* `harness_owner` MUST be `none` for `docs-only` and `verification-only`, and
  MUST be a task ID for `covered-by`.
* `exempt_verification_command` MUST be an exact, runnable command, not a description. It is
  executed verbatim in PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) from the repository root.
* `exempt_precondition` MUST be the literal `must-fail-before-deliverable`. No other value is
  recognized.
* A missing key, a key out of order, an empty value, or a placeholder value is
  `EXEMPT_CONTRACT_INCOMPLETE` — fail closed. A present-but-non-executable
  `exempt_verification_command` is `EXEMPT_COMMAND_MISSING`.

**Additional conditions for `covered-by`** — split across two gates:

*Static intake conditions* (evaluated at Ship Step 2a and harness-architect Step 1a):

* The task named in `harness_owner` exists as a task in the same release unit.
* The owner is a declared dependency of the exempt task, direct or transitive.
* The owner is **eligible** to be harness-satisfied by `harness-ready` — it does not itself carry
  `harness-exempt`. An exempt task may never be covered by another exempt task.
* `harness_owner_command` is present and exact.

*Claim-time conditions* (evaluated immediately before the exempt task is claimed, at Ship Step
4.1a — never at intake):

* The owner now carries the `harness-ready` label.
* The owner's red evidence is complete: its harness manifest records `Compilation: PASS` and
  `Red Phase: CONFIRMED` per P-004.
* The owner's harness commit has landed.

**Why the split is load-bearing.** Intake for a wave runs **before** that wave's harness
generation, so the owner's red evidence does not exist yet by construction. Evaluating the owner's
red evidence at intake makes `covered-by` unsatisfiable for every shipment whose owner harness has
not already been scaffolded, which deadlocks the shipment at its own gate. Intake therefore
validates only what is knowable statically — fields, class, reason, contract membership, owner
dependency edge, owner type, and the declared commands — and the red-evidence conditions are
re-evaluated at claim time, where they are knowable and where a missing red is still a halt before
any implementation begins.

Classes `docs-only` and `verification-only` require **no** predecessor harness owner and MUST NOT
have a test fabricated for them. A test that can only fail because a symbol does not yet exist is
a build error, and a test that passes the moment a declared shape lands was never red. Neither
statement licenses an exemption for a **declaration**: a declaration task takes the source-shape
harness described above, which is neither a build error nor a tautology.

**Evaluation order — static intake** (ship Step 2a, harness-architect Step 1a), run **once per
wave over that wave's ready set** (P-002.6):

1. Task carries `harness-ready` → harness-satisfied. Stop.
2. Task carries `harness-exempt` but has no contract block, or the block is missing a required key
   or carries an empty/placeholder value → **halt** (P-002.2 `EXEMPT_CONTRACT_INCOMPLETE`).
3. `harness_exemption_class` is missing or outside the closed vocabulary → **halt** (P-002.2
   `EXEMPT_CLASS_UNRECOGNIZED`).
4. `exempt_verification_command` is absent, empty, or not an executable command → **halt** (P-002.2
   `EXEMPT_COMMAND_MISSING`).
5. Task is absent from the declared closed exempt set → **halt** (P-002.2 `EXEMPT_NOT_IN_CONTRACT`).
6. The task's declared deliverable changes production behavior — **including landing any
   production declaration a caller can observe** — and its class is not `covered-by` → **halt**
   (P-002.2 `EXEMPT_BEHAVIOR_NO_OWNER`). Objective test in P-002.4.
7. Class is `covered-by` and any *static intake* owner condition above fails → **halt** (P-002.2
   `EXEMPT_OWNER_INVALID`).
8. Otherwise → **statically admitted**. Schedule the task in dependency order and do not scaffold a
   harness for it. Static admission is not permission to build.

**Evaluation order — claim time** (ship Step 4.1a, immediately before the task is claimed):

1. Re-read the contract block. Any drift from the statically admitted values → **halt**
   (`EXEMPT_CONTRACT_INCOMPLETE`).
2. Class is `covered-by`: the owner carries `harness-ready`, its manifest records
   `Compilation: PASS` and `Red Phase: CONFIRMED`, and its harness commit has landed. Any one
   absent → **halt** (P-002.2 `EXEMPT_OWNER_NOT_RED`). Absence is a halt, never a wait-and-proceed.
3. Run the P-002.3 pre-work precondition probe. A pre-work success → **halt** (P-002.2
   `EXEMPT_FALSE_GREEN`).
4. Otherwise → the task may be claimed and dispatched to `build-feature`.

**Producer obligation** (harness-architect), **scoped to the wave it is invoked for** (P-002.6):
Partition the **wave's** task set before scaffolding. Tasks that pass P-002.1 static intake as
`harness-exempt` are already harness-satisfied — do **not** generate red tests, stubs, or a
`harness-ready` label for them, and do not treat their absence from the `harness-ready` set as a
gap. Scaffold the non-exempt members of the wave, **including every `covered-by` owner that is in
this wave**, so that the owner's red evidence exists by the time the exempt task reaches its
claim-time gate. Tasks whose exemption fails static intake are a halt, not a scaffolding target.
Tasks outside the current wave are **out of scope for this invocation**: their dependencies are
not yet `done`, so their harnesses may not compile, and attempting them is the one-pass deadlock
P-002.6 exists to prevent.

**Preserved test-first semantics**: Every behavior-changing task that is not `covered-by` a valid,
red-confirmed predecessor still requires `harness-ready` before implementation — **including every
task whose delta is a production declaration**, which takes a source-shape harness.
`harness-exempt` never substitutes for `harness-ready` on such a task, and the harness →
implementation ordering is unchanged for all non-exempt work. Waves change *when* a harness is
scaffolded, never *whether* one is required.

### P-002.2 — Harness-Exempt Halt Taxonomy and Reporting

**Statement**: A failed exemption evaluation is a reportable P-002 gap, not a silent skip and not
a trigger for scaffolding a substitute harness. Each code names the gate that owns it, so a code
raised at the wrong gate is itself a contract defect.

| Code | Owning gate | Condition | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EXEMPT_CONTRACT_INCOMPLETE` | static intake; re-checked at claim time | Contract block absent, a required key missing or out of order, an empty or placeholder value, or drift between intake and claim time | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} harness-exemption contract block is incomplete or drifted [{detail}].` |
| `EXEMPT_CLASS_UNRECOGNIZED` | static intake | `harness_exemption_class` missing, unreadable, or outside the closed vocabulary | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} carries harness-exempt with unrecognized class [{value}].` |
| `EXEMPT_COMMAND_MISSING` | static intake | `exempt_verification_command` absent, empty, a description rather than a command, or — for `covered-by` — `harness_owner_command` absent | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} declares no executable exempt verification command.` |
| `EXEMPT_NOT_IN_CONTRACT` | static intake | Task is not a member of the declared closed exempt set in the plan, feature, or shipment contract | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} claims harness-exempt but is not in the declared exempt set for {release_unit}.` |
| `EXEMPT_BEHAVIOR_NO_OWNER` | static intake; re-checked at the completion gate | Behavior-changing implementation without a `covered-by` predecessor harness owner, per the P-002.4 objective test | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} changes behavior under harness-exempt class [{class}] with no predecessor harness owner.` |
| `EXEMPT_OWNER_INVALID` | static intake | Named owner does not exist, is not a declared dependency, or is itself `harness-exempt` | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} names harness owner {owner_id}, which is not a valid red-evidence dependency.` |
| `EXEMPT_OWNER_NOT_RED` | **claim time only** | At claim time the owner does not carry `harness-ready`, its manifest does not record `Compilation: PASS` / `Red Phase: CONFIRMED`, or its harness commit has not landed | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} would build before owner {owner_id} red evidence is confirmed.` |
| `EXEMPT_FALSE_GREEN` | claim time / build-feature entry | The pre-work run of `exempt_verification_command` succeeded before any work was done, or produced a P-002.3 false-green signal that was treated as success | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} exempt verification command passed before the deliverable existed [{command}].` |
| `EXEMPT_EVIDENCE_MISMATCH` | completion gate | Post-deliverable run exits 0 but carries a false-green signal, or does not match the declared guard count, content assertions, or evidence-manifest fields | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} exempt verification passed vacuously or did not match declared evidence [{detail}].` |
| `EXEMPT_DELTA_EXCEEDS_CLASS` | completion gate | The task's changed-file set is outside the P-002.4 class delta surface | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} changed files outside its harness-exempt class [{class}] surface: {paths}.` |
| `EXEMPT_MARKER_MISSING` | claim time / build-feature entry; re-checked at the completion gate | The command exited 0 without printing its declared `EXEMPT_VERIFY_OK:{task_id}` marker | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} exempt verification command exited 0 without its declared positive marker [{command}].` |
| `EXEMPT_COMMAND_DESTRUCTIVE` | pre-execution screening (Ship Step 4.1a; `build-feature` Step 0) | `exempt_verification_command` or `harness_owner_command` matches a Principle VII destructive-operation pattern instead of a read-only probe | `P-002 GAP: {task_id} declares a destructive exempt/harness-owner command [{command}]; routed to Principle VII approval, not executed.` |
| `WAVE_NO_PROGRESS` | **wave admission only** (Ship Step 4.0, P-002.6) | Tasks remain non-terminal but no `queued` member has all dependencies terminal, so the next wave is empty; **or** a member is still `active` at wave admission (a leftover claim from a prior wave that never completed) | `P-002 GAP: wave {n} for {release_unit} is empty with {count} member(s) still non-terminal; blocked set: {task_ids}; active residual: {task_ids}.` |
| `WAVE_MEMBER_BLOCKED` | **wave admission only** (Ship Step 4.0, P-002.6) | Any member of the frozen task wave set `M` carries status `blocked`, whether set by `return_blocked` or by any other path. A status outside the configured executable and terminal-success sets is **not** this code — it is `WAVE_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED` | `P-002 GAP: wave {n} for {release_unit} has {count} blocked member(s): {task_ids}; dependency impact: {blocked_id} -> {unreachable_dependent_ids}; return_blocked recorded: {yes\|no}.` |
| `WAVE_CYCLE_DETECTED` | **wave admission only** (Ship Step 4.0, P-002.6) | The residual blocked set contains a dependency cycle, so no wave ordering exists | `P-002 GAP: dependency cycle in {release_unit} prevents wave scheduling: {cycle_path}.` |
| `WAVE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` | **wave admission only** (Ship Step 4.0, P-002.6) | The wave counter exceeded the task count, indicating a scheduler defect rather than a graph property | `P-002 GAP: wave scheduler exceeded its {limit}-wave budget for {release_unit}; halting rather than looping.` |
| `WAVE_SNAPSHOT_UNRELIABLE` | **wave admission only** (Ship Step 4.0, P-002.6) | The per-wave status/dependency snapshot query or list call errors, returns non-parseable output, or returns a task row count that does not equal frozen `count(M)` | `P-002 GAP: wave {n} snapshot for {release_unit} is unreliable [{detail}]; expected {expected_count} task(s), observed {observed_count}.` |
| `WAVE_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED` | **wave admission only** (Ship Step 4.0, P-002.6) | A member of `M` carries a status that is in neither the configured **executable** set nor the configured **terminal-success** set — a catalog token such as `review`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `shipped`, or `abandoned`, or a token outside the catalog entirely | `P-002 GAP: wave {n} for {release_unit} has {count} member(s) in an unsupported status: {task_id}={status}, …; unsupported is never terminal and never completes.` |
| `WAVE_STATUS_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE` | **schedule construction** (Ship Step 3, P-002.6) | The configured status catalog or the registry status mapping cannot be read, is empty, or disagrees with the configured executable/terminal-success sets (a configured token absent from the catalog, or a token in both sets) | `P-002 GAP: configured status model for {release_unit} is unavailable or self-inconsistent [{detail}]; refusing to schedule against a built-in fallback vocabulary.` |
| `WAVE_MANIFEST_UNAVAILABLE` | **schedule construction** (Ship Step 3, P-002.6) | The shipment item list cannot be read; an item's type cannot be resolved; the task-type filter cannot produce `M`; non-shipment mode lacks a non-empty, duplicate-free explicit `frozen_task_ids` input; or that explicit set disagrees with filtered shipment task IDs when both are available | `P-002 GAP: cannot freeze task wave set M for {release_unit} [{detail}]; total manifest members: {manifest_count}; excluded non-task members: {id} ({type}), …; refusing to schedule against an inferred member set.` |
| `WAVE_RED_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED` | **schedule construction** (Ship Step 3, P-002.6) | A member whose declared deliverable is a red harness carries no canonical `red-deliverable-contract`; any of its five keys is absent, empty, malformed, or inconsistent; a green-maker is outside `M`, self-referential, or not strictly later; or `green_maker_closes_wave` is not the actual last green-maker wave | `P-002 GAP: red-deliverable contract for {release_unit} is missing or ambiguous: {task_ids}; refusing to infer it.` |
| `WAVE_GREEN_REGRESSION_INVALID` | **schedule construction** (Ship Step 3, P-002.6) | An optional `green-regression-contract` block is duplicated, malformed, carries keys other than `green_regression_cmds`, or contains a non-string, empty, duplicate, unscoped, or weakening command | `P-002 GAP: green-regression contract for {task_id} is invalid [{detail}]; default is the empty list and no command may be inferred from prose.` |
| `WAVE_OPEN_RED_UNCLOSED` | **wave convergence gate** (Ship Step 4.6) and **final closure** (Ship Step 5, P-002.6) | An `open_red_deliverables` entry is still open after its declared `green_maker_closes_wave`, or at final closure — including when a green-maker reached `archived` (a descope) rather than a completion status | `P-002 GAP: open red {task_id} ({selector}) is unclosed at wave {n}; declared green-maker(s) {ids} status {statuses}; the deferred full suite can never be discharged.` |
| `WAVE_RED_DELIVERABLE_EARLY_GREEN` | **wave convergence gate** (Ship Step 4.6, P-002.6); **red-deliverable execution** (`build-feature` Step 0.5a pre-landing baseline, Step 0.5d post-landing check, and Step 0.5f inverted suite) | A red deliverable's `red_selector_command` is observed **passing** while at least one declared green-maker is still not closed — whether the deliverable completed in this wave, was carried in from an earlier one, or is green at its own dispatch before it has landed anything | `P-002 GAP: red deliverable {task_id} ({selector}) is green at wave {n} but green-maker(s) {ids} status {statuses}; the ordering contract it pins is void.` |
| `WAVE_RED_DELIVERABLE_PRELANDED` | **red-deliverable execution** (`build-feature` Step 0.5a) | The declared `red_selector_command` already reports a matching `--- FAIL:` against the pre-work tree, so the harness is already present and this dispatch would re-land an existing deliverable against an empty delta | `P-002 GAP: red deliverable {task_id} ({selector}) is already landed and already red at its own dispatch; the delta would be empty.` |
| `WAVE_RED_DELIVERABLE_VACUOUS` | **red-deliverable execution** (`build-feature` Step 0.5d) | After the harness lands, `red_selector_command` still produces a P-002.3 no-tests-to-run signal at any exit code, so the selector matches no test and the observed red proves nothing | `P-002 GAP: red deliverable {task_id} ({selector}) matched no test after landing; a vacuous red is not the deliverable.` |
| `WAVE_GREEN_MAKER_UNVERIFIED` | **wave convergence gate** (Ship Step 4.6, P-002.6) | An entry in `newly_closed_k` — every declared green-maker now `done` — still has a **failing** `red_selector_command` at the gate that closed it | `P-002 GAP: green-maker(s) {ids} completed at wave {n} but open red {task_id} ({selector}) is still failing; the deferred full suite would carry an unverified red forward.` |

**`EXEMPT_OWNER_NOT_RED` is a claim-time code.** Raising it at static intake is a false halt: at
intake the harness has not been generated yet, so no owner can have red evidence. Static intake
validates the owner's existence, dependency edge, and type only.

**Violation Action**: Halt at the gate point. Record the code and message through P-005 telemetry.
Return the task to the operator or to Stage for a contract amendment. Do not scaffold a
substitute harness, do not relabel the task `harness-ready`, do not weaken or replace the declared
verification command, and do not proceed with a partial queue.

### P-002.3 — Exempt Execution Contract (Must-Fail-Before-Deliverable)

**Statement**: An exemption removes the *scaffolded red harness*, not the *observed failure*. Every
exempt task carries an executable command that MUST be observed failing before the deliverable
exists and passing after it lands. A command that cannot fail before the work is not a gate.

**Positive completion marker (mandatory), and its exact scope.** Every
`exempt_verification_command` — and **only** `exempt_verification_command` — MUST print an
explicit, task-unique positive marker: `EXEMPT_VERIFY_OK:{task_id}` (for example
`Write-Output 'EXEMPT_VERIFY_OK:147.019-T'`), as its last statement, reached only after every
preceding assertion in the command has already passed, immediately before the command's own
`exit 0`. A run counts as passing only when it exits 0 **and** the exact marker for that task is
present in captured stdout; exit 0 alone is never sufficient. This closes the cmd/shell-inversion
and no-op gap: a wrapper that negates the real exit code, a shell that swallows a failure, or a
no-op stand-in can each manufacture an unearned exit 0, but none can also emit the one
task-specific string that the command only reaches after its own guard clauses have already
returned zero.

**`harness_owner_command` is deliberately unmarked and MUST NOT carry the marker.** It is
`covered-by`'s *loop* command — the predecessor owner's scaffolded harness selector — and it is
validated by its own named `--- PASS:` count against that harness, per the
Loop-command-versus-gate-command rule below. Requiring a marker on it would require editing the
owner's harness to emit a string on the dependent's behalf, which is exactly the
harness-modification this policy forbids everywhere else. Any consumer, re-apply note, or template
that asserts a marker requirement on `harness_owner_command` is **wrong** and must be corrected
against this paragraph.

**A marker requirement is a *gate-command* rule, never a *must-fail* observation.** These are two
different roles and conflating them is what makes the gate unsound:

* At the **post-deliverable gate**, a missing or mismatched marker at exit 0 is
  `EXEMPT_MARKER_MISSING` (P-002.2) — a halt.
* At the **pre-work probe**, a missing marker at exit 0 is **also** `EXEMPT_MARKER_MISSING` — a
  halt — and is **never** counted as the required pre-work failure. See the pre-work probe rules
  below.

**Read-only screening precedes execution (P-002.5).** Before any exempt/harness-owner command is
executed at all — `exempt_verification_command` at the pre-work probe or completion gate below, or
`harness_owner_command` at the build-feature loop — it MUST first pass the P-002.5 destructive-
operation screen. A command rejected by that screen is never run here; see P-002.5.

**Pre-work probe (mandatory)**: Before executing an exempt task, Ship — and `build-feature` on
entry — runs `exempt_verification_command` **exactly once** against the pre-work tree and MUST
observe failure. Classify the run into exactly one of three outcomes; two of them halt.

1. **Required failure (proceed).** A non-zero exit status, **or** exit 0 carrying one of the
   false-green signals below from a *well-formed* command — `[no tests to run]`,
   `testing: warning: no tests to run`, `no test files`, or zero matching `--- PASS: <name>` lines
   for a named-selector command. This is the observation the gate needs. Record it as the task's
   red-equivalent evidence and proceed.
2. **Exit 0 *with* the declared marker → halt** with P-002.2 `EXEMPT_FALSE_GREEN`. The deliverable
   appears to already exist. Do not implement, do not weaken the command, and do not proceed on
   the theory that the work is already done.
3. **Exit 0 *without* the declared marker → halt** with P-002.2 `EXEMPT_MARKER_MISSING`. This is
   **not** the required failure of outcome 1 and MUST NOT be counted as one. P-002.3 requires the
   marker as the command's last statement before its own `exit 0`, so an unmarked exit 0 means the
   command is **malformed** — it proves nothing about the tree, in either direction. Return the
   task for a contract amendment. Proceeding here would let a no-op or inverted wrapper satisfy
   the must-fail precondition, which is the precise gap the marker exists to close.

Outcome 3 is a halt at **both** gates. A missing marker is always `EXEMPT_MARKER_MISSING` and is
never admissible as evidence of failure, of success, or of anything else. Ship Step 4.1a item 4
and `build-feature` Step 0 item 4 state the same three-way classification and are the
consumer-side mirrors of this rule.

**False-green signals** (each is a failure of a *well-formed* command regardless of exit status;
each therefore counts as the required pre-work failure in outcome 1, and each is
`EXEMPT_EVIDENCE_MISMATCH` at the post-deliverable gate):

| Signal | Where it comes from | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `[no tests to run]` | `go test -run <selector>` with a selector that matches nothing | Failure. `go test` exits 0 in this case, so exit status alone is not admissible evidence. |
| `testing: warning: no tests to run` | the same case under `-v` | Failure. |
| `no test files` | a package with no `_test.go` files | Failure. |
| zero matching `--- PASS: <name>` lines | `go test -v` with a named-selector command | Failure. A selector command MUST assert a minimum count of named `--- PASS:` lines equal to the number of guards the task declares. |
| a no-op or vacuously-true content probe | a docs or evidence probe whose assertions are all satisfied by the pre-work tree | Failure at authoring time: the command is not a gate and MUST be strengthened, not accepted. |

A missing `EXEMPT_VERIFY_OK:{task_id}` marker at exit 0 is deliberately **absent** from this
table. It is not a false-green signal and not a must-fail observation — it is the malformed-command
halt `EXEMPT_MARKER_MISSING`, defined in the pre-work probe rules above and in the P-002.2
taxonomy. Listing it here would make an unmarked exit 0 satisfy the must-fail precondition, which
contradicts both.

**Post-deliverable gate**: After the deliverable lands, the same command MUST exit 0, print the
exact declared `EXEMPT_VERIFY_OK:{task_id}` marker, **and** carry no other false-green signal
**and** match the task's declared evidence — the named guard count, the declared content
assertions, or the declared evidence-manifest fields. Success produced by absent tests, an empty
selector, a skipped package, a no-op, or a missing marker is not a pass; report P-002.2
`EXEMPT_EVIDENCE_MISMATCH` (or `EXEMPT_MARKER_MISSING` when only the marker is absent) and halt.

**Command authoring rules by class**:

| Class | The command MUST | It MUST NOT |
|---|---|---|
| `docs-only` | Probe the required documentation or instruction **content** (the required strings, and where the deliverable replaces a claim, the absence of the replaced string) **and then** run the doc lint gate | Be the lint gate alone, which passes on the pre-work tree |
| `verification-only` | Assert the declared evidence exists — named `--- PASS:` guard lines by count, or the declared evidence-manifest rows and scalars | Rely on a selector's exit status, or accept a manifest file that exists but lacks the required fields |
| `covered-by` | Assert the owner's harness selector passes by named `--- PASS:` count **and** probe this task's own final deliverable | Be the owner's selector alone when the task has its own deliverable to pin |

A **declaration** task has no row here because it is not exempt (see P-002.1). Its gate is a
normal red harness: a source-shape (`go/ast`) harness that compiles before the declaration lands,
fails on assertion, and is driven green by the implementation.

**Loop command versus gate command**: For `covered-by`, the implementation loop runs
`harness_owner_command` (the owner's failing harness, driven from red to green) and the completion
gate runs `exempt_verification_command`. For every other class the two are the same command. The
`EXEMPT_VERIFY_OK:{task_id}` marker is required on the **gate** command in both cases and on the
**loop** command in neither.

**Violation Action**: Halt at the gate point, record the P-002.2 code through P-005 telemetry, and
return the task for a contract amendment. Never relax the command to make the gate pass.

### P-002.4 — Objective Behavior Classification and Class Delta Surface

**Statement**: `covered-by` is the **only** exempt class that may modify production behavior. The
other two classes MUST NOT. Classification is decided against the actual changed-file set and
delta, not against the task's prose, and the check fails closed when the actual change exceeds the
class.

**Class delta surface** — the changed-file set for an exempt task's commit MUST be a subset of:

| Class | Allowed changed files | Hard prohibitions |
|---|---|---|
| `docs-only` | Markdown, instruction, prompt, and agent artifacts only | Zero `*.go` files changed, test or production |
| `verification-only` | New or appended `*_test.go` files and evidence artifacts under `docs/closure/` | Zero non-test `*.go` files changed; **no repository-configuration file** — `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, CI config, or build config — of any kind |
| `covered-by` | Non-test production files named in the task | No `*_test.go` file added or modified — the owner owns the harness |

**`verification-only` is not a repository-hygiene class.** A verification task that needs a scratch
workspace MUST place it under a path that is **already** ignored by the committed `.gitignore` —
verified with `git check-ignore -v <path>`, not assumed — so the task commits no ignore rule and
leaves no dirty tree behind. If no already-ignored path is suitable, the ignore rule is a
**separate, non-exempt workspace-hygiene task** with its own red harness or probe. Widening this
class to admit configuration files is forbidden: it would reopen the `EXEMPT_BEHAVIOR_NO_OWNER`
boundary and make the class surface unfalsifiable.

**Baseline definition**: `exempt_baseline_sha` is the commit SHA of the working tree **immediately
before the task is claimed and before any mutation** — captured by Ship at Step 4.1a, after the
must-fail probe and before Step 4.1b, as `git rev-parse HEAD`. It is recorded with the pre-work
probe output and passed unchanged to `build-feature`, so the gate and the loop measure the same
delta. There is no implicit or inferred baseline: if `exempt_baseline_sha` is absent, unrecorded,
or disagrees between Ship and `build-feature`, **halt** with `EXEMPT_DELTA_EXCEEDS_CLASS` rather
than guessing a range.

**Diff form depends on whether the task's commit exists yet (mandatory).** The two consumers of
this rule run the gate at **different points in the commit lifecycle**, so they MUST use different
right-hand sides. Getting this wrong makes the gate vacuous rather than strict, which is the worst
possible failure mode for a fail-closed check:

| Consumer | Runs | Correct diff form | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build-feature` post-loop completion gate | **before** the skill's own `### Commit` step | `git diff --name-only {exempt_baseline_sha}` and `git diff {exempt_baseline_sha} -- <file>` (two-dot, **no right-hand side**), plus the `--cached` form so staged changes are included | The task's work is staged/unstaged in the **working tree** and not yet in `HEAD`. Omitting the right-hand side diffs the baseline commit against the working tree, which is the only range that contains the delta at that moment. |
| Ship Step 4.3 quality gates | **after** `build-feature` reports success and after its commit | `git diff --name-only {exempt_baseline_sha}..HEAD` and `git diff {exempt_baseline_sha}..HEAD -- <file>` | The commit exists by then, so `HEAD` is the correct right-hand side and the range is stable. |

**A `{exempt_baseline_sha}..HEAD` diff evaluated before the task's commit exists compares the
baseline against itself, yields an empty delta, and passes both passes trivially.** That is not a
pass — it is an absent gate. A completion gate that observes an **empty** changed-file set MUST
**halt** with `EXEMPT_DELTA_EXCEEDS_CLASS` (detail: `empty delta — gate ran outside the range that
contains the task's work`) rather than reporting success. An exempt task that legitimately changed
nothing has no deliverable and cannot have passed its post-deliverable gate, so the empty case is
always a defect somewhere.

**Evidence rule**: At the completion gate, run two passes against `exempt_baseline_sha`, using the
diff form from the table above for the consumer running them. Both must pass, and neither may be
empty; a filename pass alone is not sufficient, because the class surfaces above are content
restrictions and not merely path restrictions.

1. **Path pass** — the `--name-only` form, compared against the class surface above.
   * An **empty** result → **halt** with `EXEMPT_DELTA_EXCEEDS_CLASS` (vacuous gate), per the rule
     above.
   * Any changed file outside the class surface → **halt** with P-002.2 `EXEMPT_DELTA_EXCEEDS_CLASS`.
   * Any non-test `*.go` change under `docs-only` or `verification-only` → **halt** with
     `EXEMPT_BEHAVIOR_NO_OWNER`: the delta is behavior under a class that admits none.
   * Any `*_test.go` change under `covered-by` → **halt** with `EXEMPT_DELTA_EXCEEDS_CLASS`.
2. **Content pass** — the per-file diff form for this consumer (`git diff {exempt_baseline_sha} --
   <each allowed file>` before the commit; `git diff {exempt_baseline_sha}..HEAD -- <each allowed
   file>` after it), inspecting the hunks themselves. A file being inside the surface does not make
   its contents admissible.
   * `verification-only`: every hunk must be in a `*_test.go` file or a `docs/closure/` artifact,
     and no hunk may weaken, delete, rename, or narrow the selector of a pre-existing assertion.
     A hunk in `.gitignore` or any other repository-configuration file → **halt** with
     `EXEMPT_DELTA_EXCEEDS_CLASS`.
   * `docs-only`: no `*.go` hunk of any kind.
   * `covered-by`: no `*_test.go` hunk of any kind; production hunks are unrestricted in shape
     because the owner's red harness is what constrains them.

When the `agent-engram` capability pack is installed, `list_symbols` or `impact_analysis` over the
changed files is the preferred way to establish whether a hunk altered a pre-existing function body
before falling back to reading the raw diff.

Fail closed: when the delta cannot be attributed to a class surface — an unclassifiable path, a
mixed commit, an absent or disputed baseline, or an unreadable diff — halt rather than admitting it.

### P-002.5 — Read-Only Command Screening (Principle VII Routing)

**Statement**: `exempt_verification_command` and `harness_owner_command` are read-only probes that
assert and report; they are never mutating actions. Before Ship or `build-feature` executes either
command — at Ship Step 4.1a and at `build-feature` Step 0, the two points that ever run them —
the command text MUST be statically screened for a destructive-operation pattern under Constitution
Principle VII: file or directory deletion, force-overwrite without backup, system or repository
configuration mutation, version-control history alteration, data drops or truncation, installation
or removal of a system-level package, or execution of untrusted or remote code.

**Screening outcome**:

* A command matching no destructive pattern is read-only and MAY be executed as the pre-work probe
  or completion gate.
* A command matching a destructive pattern is **rejected outright** and is never executed by this
  gate — approved or not. Report P-002.2 `EXEMPT_COMMAND_DESTRUCTIVE` and route the command through
  Constitution Principle VII's operator-approval path; only a human-approved, manually-run action
  may proceed from there, entirely outside this automated gate.

**Authoring rule**: an `exempt_verification_command` or `harness_owner_command` MUST assert and
report only — for example `go doc`, `go test -run` (with its named `--- PASS:` count), `go vet`,
`Test-Path`, `Get-Content`, `Select-String`, `git rev-parse`, `git diff --name-only`, or a read-only
`go run ./cmd/backlogit … docs lint`. It MUST NOT delete, move, overwrite, rewrite history, drop or
truncate data, install or remove a package, or invoke untrusted code. A command that needs a
mutating step to prove its deliverable is not a valid exempt gate — the mutation belongs to the
implementation the gate observes, never to the gate itself.

**Violation Action**: Reject the command without executing it, record `EXEMPT_COMMAND_DESTRUCTIVE`
through P-005 telemetry, and return the task for a contract amendment. Do not weaken the screen to
admit a destructive command, and do not execute it "once, carefully" outside the Principle VII
approval path.
